claim: Replacing the constant start with a fine symmetric unimodal profile (N=64 log-parametrized heights, L-BFGS-B) raises R from 0.6667 to 0.7552; the optimum is a smooth central bump with positive nonuniform wings (max/mean height 1.62) and a flatter f*f top (1% share 9.3%).

Simulated annealing over N=32 heights with multiplicative/block/swap moves, seeded from an upsampled tent, reaches R=0.8404, far above symmetric local search; the resulting profile is asymmetric (max/mean 2.59, f*f peak at 0.562) and much flatter near the top (1% share 30.8%).

Random hill-climbing on N=400 heights seeded with a Gaussian bump reaches R=0.8648, the best of generation 1; the profile is strongly asymmetric (max/mean 3.53, f*f peak at 0.170) with a very flat f*f top (1% share 41.3%).

Coordinate-wise local search on upsampled heights (N=7680) reaches R=0.7938, beating short symmetric families but below the asymmetric SA/hill-climb results; its f*f peak sits at 0.581 with 1% share 21.1%.

Multiscale multiplicative hill-climbing with adaptive resolution (N=33925) reaches R=0.8106; the profile is nearly symmetric in mass (max/mean 1.80) but the f*f peak is off-center at 0.252, showing asymmetry helps even at high resolution.

All generation-1 winners are asymmetric with an off-center f*f peak (0.17-0.58), and higher R correlates with flatter f*f tops (1% share 9%->41%). Worth testing whether explicitly optimizing for a flat, off-center f*f plateau (rather than generic hill-climbing) pushes R above 0.865, and whether the true optimum is a one-sided ramp.

Replacing the Gaussian-bump seed with a discretized x^{-p} power-singularity seed (left/right/symmetric, n up to 800, p up to 0.8) inside the same hill-climb raised R from 0.8648 to 0.8743 (+0.0095); the winning profile is strongly asymmetric (max/mean 6.32) with a much flatter f*f top (1% share 42.5% vs 41.3%) and its f*f peak at 0.482. Upsampling the N=400 winner to N=2000 and adding edge-sharpening, log-block multiplicative, and re-interpolation moves barely moved R (0.8648 -> 0.8658, +0.0010). Resolution and edge moves are not the binding constraint: the shape family, not the search resolution, limits R, since the result stays near the smooth-bump basin (max/mean 3.51, f*f peak 0.424).

Gradient-based refinement of the smooth-bump basin does not escape it: analytic-gradient ascent plus hill-climbing (p0008, N=400) gave only 0.8683 (+0.0035) and L-BFGS-B in log-height space with multi-scale growth to N=4000 (p0013) gave only 0.8654 (+0.0005). Multi-resolution local search with upsampling and smooth multiplicative moves, run wide from the N=32 SA winner, produced no gain (0.84045 -> 0.84047, +0.00002). At N=32 the SA basin is already locally saturated for this move set; the wide-loop mutation did not change the shape family or resolution enough to matter.

The x^{-1/2} algebra predicts R near 0.90 for a discretized singular edge, but the best generation-2 result is 0.8808 (p0012) and the raw singular seed only 0.8743 (p0010). Freeing the exponent and raising the log-modulation to degree 8 (11 params, multi-start Nelder-Mead+L-BFGS-B at N=1200, scored to N=8000) gave zero gain over p0012 (0.880755 -> 0.880755). Family stiffness is not the binding constraint on the ~0.88 plateau; the richer family just re-converges to the same shape.

Direct log-space L-BFGS-B over all N heights with an exact analytic gradient, started inside p0012's singular-edge basin (N=2000 then 4000), gained only +0.0008 (0.880755 -> 0.881554). The parametric ansatz is not the limiter: the singular-edge basin is locally saturated for free-form gradient ascent, so the ~0.02 gap to the ~0.90 algebra bound is not a stiffness or parametrization artifact.

Adding a second power singularity at the right end (a*u^-p + b*(1-u)^-q + c, multi-start Nelder-Mead/L-BFGS-B at N=2000, rebuilt to N=8000) gained only +0.0008 (0.880755 -> 0.881554). Two-edge structure does not beat the single x^{-1/2} edge, so the single-edge ansatz is not structurally wrong.

Multi-resolution projected gradient ascent with an analytic gradient of R, plus adaptive step/restart, from p0012 at N=1000 gave only +0.0001 (0.880755 -> 0.880875). Gradient ascent on the singular-edge basin is saturated regardless of step control.

Direct analytic-gradient ascent on step heights with progressive upsampling (800->12800), smoothing and perturbed restarts, from p0012, produced no gain (0.880755 -> 0.880755). Upsampling and perturbation do not escape the singular-edge basin, consistent with resolution not being the constraint.

All four generation-3 attacks on the ~0.88 plateau (richer family, free-form gradient, two-edge, multi-resolution ascent) land within +0.0008 of p0012, so the ~0.02 gap to the ~0.90 algebra bound is not stiffness, parametrization, or single-edge structure. Replacing p0019's two-edge family with a vanishing right edge u^{-p}(1-u)^q exp(quartic) (9 params, multi-start NM+L-BFGS-B at N=2000, then free-form log-space polish to N=4000) gained only +0.00009 (0.881554 -> 0.881645). The vanishing-edge tail structure does not break the ~0.8816 plateau; the jump edge is effectively optimal for this objective.

A perturbed-restart loop (block/full log-normal noise sigma 0.1-0.3, L-BFGS-B, periodic N=8000 polish, run to 0.9*budget) from p0015 found no escape: best 0.881619 (+0.00007). The 0.8816 level is a local max of the free-form problem under this perturbation scale, not a budget-limited artifact.

Resolving the singular edge at N=10000 then 20000 with FFT-accelerated convolution and log-space L-BFGS-B gave only +0.00007 (0.881554 -> 0.881620), and the run used just 2.0 s of 30 s. Finite-N quadrature is not the binding constraint; the continuum optimum near the singular-edge basin is ~0.8816.

Progressive multistage resolution refinement (2000->20000) with exact L-BFGS-B gradient, continuing until the deadline rather than stopping early, gave the best generation-4 result: 0.881681 (+0.00013 over p0015). The gain is marginal but real, and the f*f peak landed at 0.448 (vs 0.057 for p0015), confirming the plateau is reachable from multiple f*f-peak positions.

Gradient ascent with momentum, extra upsample stages, and larger perturbation kicks from p0012 reached only 0.880922 (+0.00017). Momentum and kicks do not escape the singular-edge basin; the ~0.88 level is robust to this class of moves.
